item.title: Replay Versus Reality
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: When Referees Can Hit Rewind Though I’ve never been much interested in sports, I recollect the early days of instant replay. When a disputed play occurred, referees could review what happened and, sometimes, revise a call. Was there a foul? Did the basketball shot leave the air in time to be counted? Did the baseball player’s foot actually touch home plate? Instead of debating it in circles, instant replay offered something unprecedented: the option of seeing what really happened.

item.title: Reclaiming our Attention (and our Inbox)
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: In recent news, Meta and YouTube were found guilty of designing addictive products that harmed young people. There’s no doubt of the validity of that claim. However, they aren’t the only organizations responsible for co-opting attention. My own attention deficit journey began this morning. I had nearly 3,000 unread emails in my inbox. What to do? I looked at them the way you might look at a crime scene: who were the potential suspects?

item.title: Distractions, attention, and focus
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: It was a beautiful winter night to take our dog out for a walk. Looking toward the west I saw the planetary alignment my wife had told me about earlier that day. I immediately pulled out my phone to capture a picture. But, the picture didn’t look just right. So, I opened a browser window to see what settings to adjust for night shots. I must have messed with my phone settings for ten minutes before the ridiculousness of the situation dawned on me.
